Subject: Dedicated capacity question — H100/A100/L4 tradeoffs

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this—quick summary of where we are: CoralX has two production models we want to host on Dedicated: a long-context conversational model (approx. 70B parameters, ~110GB FP32 resident size; quantized/serving footprint ~36–44GB with KV cache) and a shorter summarization model (7B-ish, ~12GB footprint). Peak concurrent sessions are ~120, average concurrent ~42; token throughput spikes up to ~2.5M tokens/hr during promo windows.

Our primary constraints are:
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 250ms for short requests; 99th <= 700ms for long context (we can tolerate higher p99 for longest flows)
- Memory headroom to support KV cache + multi-tenant residency for pinned sessions
- A cost target that keeps Dedicated unit economics better than self-hosting (aim: <= 30% uplift vs raw cloud GPU cost)

Questions: given these profiles, what would Redwood recommend for a Dedicated fleet mix (H100 vs A100 vs L4)? We're especially worried about memory-bound long-context allocation vs throughput for many small requests. Any suggested fallthrough/fallback policy and sizing for an initial 6–12 month commit would be helpful.

Attached: CoralX_ML_profile.csv (very rough telemetry and model footprints).

Cheers,
Emma
Emma Jones
ML Platform Lead, CoralX Labs

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question — H100/A100/L4 tradeoffs

Hi Emma — thanks for the detail and the CSV; that was really helpful. High level recommendation up-front: mixed-fleet with a memory-first core (H100) for long-context stateful sessions, A100s for higher-density batch/throughput, and an L4 pool for low-cost burst/embeddings and fallback for short, stateless requests.

Suggested Tier 0 (memory-first):
- 6 x H100 (each H100 reserved for pinned long-context slots). Rationale: H100’s larger HBM and multi-instance capability gives us predictable KV cache residency and room for 70B-style sessions.

Tier 1 (throughput):
- 18 x A100 (40GB or 80GB depending on local availability; we usually recommend 80GB A100 for model packing but can use 40GB with more conservative slotting). Rationale: A100 provides better cost/throughput for mid-size models and is a good fit for the 7B summarization model at scale.

Tier 2 (burst/embeddings):
- 36 x L4 (for low-latency embeddings, cheap batched generation and as a burst pool). Rationale: L4 is highly cost-efficient for short requests and can soak spikes while preserving H100 headroom.

Fallthrough and routing policy (proposal):
- Prefer sloting to H100 for sessions flagged as "stateful"/long-context up to a configured TTL (e.g., 48–72 hours).
- If H100 capacity exhausted, route to A100 with auto-quantized model variant (FP16/4-bit) preserving correctness; only route to L4 for non-critical, short contexts (e.g., offline summarization, embeddings).
- KV prefix caching: enable prefix-level cache on H100 and A100; L4 should not be used for pinned KV residency.

Cost/commit framing:
- This initial mix keeps a balance: memory headroom for high-SLO stateful traffic while letting A100/L4 handle bulk token volume. We’ll run a 6-week ramp and collect token-latency profiles; we can adjust counts and enable autoscale burst if utilization shows different patterns.

I’ll loop Dev and Karthik on the sizing assumptions and cost math (attached proposal v1 has ballpark cost numbers). If you can share a preferred start date and whether you need EU-only isolation (VPC + data residency), we’ll finalize the SOW.

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 28 Jul 2028 14:22:00 +0100
Subject: FW: CoralX dedicated: mixed-fleet sizing & memory-first fallthrough — cost assumptions and request for input

Dev / Karthik — forwarding Emma’s ask and my initial recommendation. Key open points where I need your input before I lock the SOW: 

1) H100 count sensitivity: I put 6 H100s as memory-first. Could we justify slicing H100 (2x or 3x MIG-like partitioning) for CoralX long-context sessions, or do we keep them whole for KV and residency? Thoughts on support for multi-instance on our runtime for deterministic p99?

2) A100 flavor: do we recommend 80GB A100s (better for model packing) or prioritize more 40GB instances and increase count? Emma’s file suggests many medium sessions; packing could materially cut A100 count but make fallthrough logic more complex.

3) L4 burst economics: I used 36 L4s for spike coverage. Is that aligned with our current Dedicated burst SLA (we usually keep a shared cross-customer L4 pool for short-notice spikes)? Any constraints for EU-resident hardware?

Quick numbers below for tradeoff modeling (please call out if any assumptions are off):
- Concurrent pinned long-context sessions (reserved in H100): 48 sessions at 70% avg residency (assume 0.75 slots per session with KV cache).
- Average token/hour baseline: 800k tokens/hr (outside peaks) — A100s + L4s should handle majority.
- Peak token/hr target: 2.5M (we need headroom for 2x sustained spike for 30–60m windows).

If we keep H100=6 but enable autoscale burst of +2 H100-equivalent capacity (via beefed A100 packing + quicker fallback), does that reduce committed H100 ask? I'd prefer to present 2 options to the customer: 
A) Memory-first conservative: 6 H100 / 18 A100 / 36 L4 (higher commit, simpler guarantees)
B) Hedged commit: 4 H100 / 26 A100 / 48 L4 + aggressive A100 packing + burst L4 pool (lower H100 cap, more complexity but better unit economics)

Please reply with rough feasibility by EOD so I can finalize cost math and SOW.

Thanks — Naomi

Emma / Liam — following internal alignment, attaching a short SOW draft and two sizing options so you can choose a path that matches your risk/cost profile. Summary below; full numbers in attached SOW-draft-CoralX.pdf.

Option 1 — Memory-first (recommended for tight latency & pinned sessions):
- 6 x H100 (reserved)
- 18 x A100 (reserved)
- 36 x L4 (burst + embeddings)
- Routing: pinned sessions -> H100; overflow -> A100 (quantized) -> L4 (stateless only)
- Notes: Simplest from an SLO standpoint; higher committed spend but stronger p99 guarantees for long-context.

Option 2 — Cost-hedged (lower H100 commit, more packing):
- 4 x H100 (reserved)
- 26 x A100 (reserved, 80GB preferred)
- 48 x L4 (larger burst pool)
- Routing: same policy but relies on quick A100 packing and fast fallback orchestration; slightly higher operational tuning during ramp.

Action items / next steps:
1) Please confirm which option you prefer and preferred go-live (we recommend 2028-09-15 to allow procurement lead time).
